papers.title: HyLnc: a hybrid deep learning and feature-based approach for long non-coding RNA prediction.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play important roles in gene regulation, development and disease, yet accurate identification of lncRNAs from transcriptomic data remains a major computational challenge. Existing methods often rely either on handcrafted sequence features or deep learning approaches, each with inherent limitations in capturing the full complexity of RNA sequences. In this study, we proposed HyLnc, a computational framework that integrates transformer-based contextual embeddings with biologically meaningful sequence features for improved lncRNA prediction. A custom BERT-based mode
papers.summary: HyLnc is a computational framework that combines transformer-based contextual embeddings with handcrafted biological sequence features to predict long non-coding RNAs from transcriptomic data. The hybrid approach aims to overcome limitations of methods relying solely on either handcrafted features or deep learning, improving prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Pan-cancer screening and integrative multi-omics and deep learning reveal the prognostic significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prognostic relevance of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-colorectal cancer (CRC) shared host-microbe signatures in non-intestinal epithelial malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and biological significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe interactome signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA).
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a host-microbe interaction signature previously linked to inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer also has prognostic value in bladder urothelial carcinoma. Using pan-cancer screening combined with multi-omics integration and deep learning, the authors identify and validate this shared signature as a biologically and prognostically relevant factor in BLCA.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) under both redocking and cross-docking conditions on three Alzheimer's disease targets. The authors find that the two paradigms rely on distinct determinants of success, with AI methods excelling in some cross-docking scenarios while physics-based tools remain competitive or superior in others. The work highlights that realistic cross-docking evaluation is essential for fairly assessing binding pose prediction methods.

papers.title: Multimodal alignment improves generalizability of genomic biomarker prediction in computational pathology.
papers.abstract: Computational pathology models that use digitized histopathology whole-slide images have the potential to become a cost-effective and scalable alternative to molecular assays for the prediction of genomic biomarkers, a key task in precision oncology. However, as new genomic biomarkers are discovered or quantified, large, labeled datasets must be prospectively collected to train new models. To address this challenge, we developed multimodal alignment for biomarker learning and generalization (MARBLE), a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that integrates structured biomarker knowledge i
papers.summary: MARBLE is a multimodal contrastive pretraining strategy that aligns histopathology whole-slide images with structured genomic biomarker knowledge to improve prediction of genomic biomarkers in computational pathology. The approach aims to enhance generalizability, allowing models to predict newly discovered or quantified biomarkers without requiring large prospectively collected labeled datasets.

papers.title: Multi-Sequence Fusion MRI Deep Learning Models for Discrimination of Recurrent Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma and Osteoradionecrosis.
papers.abstract: To develop a multi-sequence fusion model based on MRI images to differentiate between recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma (rNPC) and osteoradionecrosis (ORN) in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) after radiotherapy, and to evaluate its diagnostic performance.
papers.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This study develops a deep learning model that fuses multiple MRI sequences to distinguish recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma from osteoradionecrosis in patients who previously received radiotherapy for NPC. The model's diagnostic performance is evaluated, aiming to address a clinically challenging differential diagnosis where the two conditions can look similar on imaging.

papers.title: Enhancing detection of polygenic adaptation: a comparative study of machine learning and statistical approaches using simulated evolve-and-resequence data.
papers.abstract: Detecting signals of polygenic adaptation remains a significant challenge in population genomics, as traditional methods often struggle to identify the associated subtle, multi-locus allele-frequency shifts. Here, we introduced and tested several novel approaches combining machine learning techniques with traditional statistical tests to detect polygenic adaptation patterns in time-series of allele frequency changes from whole genome data. We implemented a Naive Bayesian Classifier (NBC) and One-Class Support Vector Machines (OCSVM), and compared their performance against the classical Fisher'
papers.summary: This study compares machine learning methods (Naive Bayes classifier and one-class SVM) against traditional statistical tests for detecting polygenic adaptation in simulated evolve-and-resequence time-series data. The authors find that combining ML approaches with classical tests can improve detection of subtle, multi-locus allele-frequency shifts that traditional methods miss. The work provides a benchmark for method selection in population genomics studies of polygenic adaptation.

papers.title: A Dual-Mode In Situ EV-miRNA Profiling Platform for Machine-Learning-Assisted Gastric Cancer Liquid Biopsy.
papers.abstract: EV-miRNAs are promising gastric cancer (GC) biomarkers for early diagnosis, yet their clinical application is limited by major detection challenges arising from the low abundance and high sequence homology of EV-miRNAs. Herein, we developed a dual-mode platform for sensitive EV-miRNA in situ profiling based on liposome-encapsulated localized exponential catalytic hairpin assembly (L-LECHA). L-LECHA enables the localized exponential catalytic hairpin assembly system to be delivered into EVs and activates exponential signal amplification, resulting in sensitive and rapid detection of EV-miRNAs.
papers.summary: The authors developed a dual-mode platform called L-LECHA that uses liposome-encapsulated catalytic hairpin assembly to amplify signals inside extracellular vesicles, enabling sensitive in situ profiling of low-abundance EV-miRNAs. Combined with machine learning, this approach was applied to gastric cancer liquid biopsy, addressing challenges of low abundance and high sequence homology among EV-miRNAs.

papers.title: H&E to recurrence score: A step forward, but not yet a substitute for genomic testing.
papers.abstract: Shamai and colleagues developed a multimodal deep-learning model that predicts Oncotype DX recurrence scores from routine H&E slides and clinicopathological variables in hormone receptor‑positive, HER2‑negative early breast cancer. Validated across the TAILORx trial and six external cohorts (over 5000 patients), the model achieved an AUC of 0.898 for identifying recurrence score ≥26 and recapitulated genomic assay patterns of chemotherapy benefit. Notably, 31% of clinically high-risk postmenopausal women were downgraded to low risk by AI, suggesting potential to reduce overtreatment. However,
papers.summary: Shamai and colleagues built a multimodal deep-learning model that predicts Oncotype DX recurrence scores directly from routine H&E slides plus clinicopathological variables in HR-positive, HER2-negative early breast cancer. Validated on the TAILORx trial and six external cohorts (>5000 patients), it reached AUC 0.898 for recurrence score ≥26 and downgraded 31% of clinically high-risk postmenopausal women to low risk. The editorial cautions that this is a promising step toward reducing overtreatment but not yet a replacement for genomic testing.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Hydroxytyrosol Targeting of the TXNIP-NLRP3 Inflammasome Axis in Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) induces secondary neuroinflammation driven by oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, and immune remodeling, yet specific mechanism-guided pharmacological interventions remain limited. This study established an artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated network pharmacology and multi-omics framework to evaluate whether hydroxytyrosol (HT), an olive-derived natural polyphenol, may regulate TBI-related neuroinflammatory targets centered on the TXNIP/NLRP3 inflammasome axis. Starting from the SMILES structure of HT, potential targets were predicted using PharmMapper,
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study uses an AI-integrated network pharmacology and multi-omics framework to investigate whether hydroxytyrosol, an olive-derived polyphenol, can modulate neuroinflammation after traumatic brain injury. The analysis identifies the TXNIP-NLRP3 inflammasome axis as a central target of hydroxytyrosol, suggesting a potential mechanism-guided therapeutic approach for TBI.

papers.title: Few-shot neuromorphic vision in a nonlinear photonic network laser.
papers.abstract: With the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence (AI), demand increases for hardware that mimics the brain's ability to extract structure from limited data. In the retina, ganglion cells detect features from sparse inputs via lateral inhibition, where neurons antagonistically suppress activity of neighboring cells. Biological neurons exhibit diverse heterogeneous nonlinear responses, linked to robust learning and strong performance in low-data regimes. Here, we introduce a retinally inspired photonic computing system where spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser act as
papers.summary: This paper introduces a photonic computing system that mimics retinal lateral inhibition using spatially competing lasing modes in a random network laser. The system leverages heterogeneous nonlinear responses to achieve few-shot learning, extracting structure from limited data much like biological neurons. It demonstrates a hardware approach to neuromorphic vision that performs well in low-data regimes.

papers.title: The fitness landscape of a form II rubisco in a photosynthetic bacterium guides engineering of oxygen tolerance.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (rubisco) is an important but challenging protein engineering target. Fast and selective rubiscos could enhance photosynthesis in plants and accelerate biobased production processes. To facilitate engineering of rubisco, we applied an in vivo screen that couples rubisco activity to growth rate of the photoautotrophic cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803. We screened a barcoded mutagenesis library of the form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. containing 15,000 single-site and multi-site variants. Exchanges in loop 6 near the active site, at the
papers.summary: Researchers screened a library of 15,000 variants of a form II rubisco from Gallionella sp. in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis, coupling rubisco activity to growth rate to map its fitness landscape. They identified key mutations, particularly in loop 6 near the active site, that influence catalytic activity and oxygen tolerance, providing a guide for engineering improved rubisco enzymes.

papers.title: Squidly harnesses enzyme functional hierarchy and contrastive learning to efficiently predict catalytic residues from sequence.
papers.abstract: Enzymes present a sustainable alternative to traditional chemical industries, drug synthesis, and bioremediation applications. Because catalytic residues are the key amino acids that drive enzyme function, their accurate prediction facilitates enzyme function prediction. Sequence similarity-based approaches such as BLAST are fast but require previously annotated homologues. Machine-learning (ML) approaches aim to overcome this limitation; however, current gold-standard ML-based methods require high-quality 3D structures limiting their application to large datasets. To address these challenges,
papers.summary: Squidly is a new machine-learning method that predicts which amino acids in an enzyme are catalytic directly from sequence, without requiring 3D structures. It combines a hierarchical representation of enzyme function with contrastive learning to improve accuracy and efficiency, addressing the limitations of both BLAST-based homology approaches and structure-dependent ML methods.

papers.title: LLM-guided prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity under data-limited conditions.
papers.abstract: Riboswitches are RNA regulatory elements that sense small molecules and regulate gene expression through ligand-induced conformational changes in an aptamer domain. They enable synthetic biology applications such as biosensing and gene circuit design. Accurate prediction of riboswitch-ligand binding affinity, quantified by the dissociation constant (Kd), is essential for rational riboswitch engineering. We present a neuro-symbolic framework in which LLM-derived embeddings encode riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations into a unified representation that captures r
papers.summary: This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic framework that uses LLM-derived embeddings to predict riboswitch-ligand binding affinity (Kd) by encoding riboswitch sequences, secondary structures, and ligand representations into a unified representation. The approach is designed to work under data-limited conditions, addressing a common bottleneck in riboswitch engineering for synthetic biology applications.

papers.title: Mapping the combinatorial coding between olfactory receptors and perception with deep learning.
papers.abstract: The sense of smell remains poorly understood compared with vision and audition. At its core is an information flow in which odorant molecules activate subsets of olfactory receptors (ORs) and combinations of receptor activations encode distinct percepts. However, predicting molecule-OR interactions, and linking them to perception, remains difficult. Here, we develop MolOR, an approach that maps odorants to their OR-activation profiles and then predicts their odor percepts. Using cross-attention between a graph neural network over molecules and protein-language-model embeddings of receptors, we
papers.summary: The authors developed MolOR, a deep learning approach that predicts which olfactory receptors are activated by a given odorant molecule and then uses those activation profiles to predict the resulting smell percept. It combines a graph neural network for molecules with protein language model embeddings for receptors via cross-attention, helping bridge the gap between chemical structure and odor perception.

papers.title: Topologically distinct intratumoral heterogeneity scores for predicting high-risk pathological grades in invasive lung adenocarcinoma: A multicenter study across four institutions.
papers.abstract: High-risk subtypes of invasive lung adenocarcinoma (IAC), particularly micropapillary- or solid-predominant patterns, are closely associated with poor prognosis. This multicenter retrospective study developed and validated a predictive model for the preoperative identification of these high-risk subtypes using topologically distinct intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores derived from CT images. The study included 1,051 patients with IAC. Two complementary ITH scores were developed: a two-dimensional ITH score, which integrated local radiomics features with global pixel distribution patterns o
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed and validated a CT-based radiomics model using two complementary intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) scores to preoperatively predict high-risk pathological subtypes (micropapillary- or solid-predominant) of invasive lung adenocarcinoma in 1,051 patients. The approach integrates local radiomic features with global pixel distribution patterns, offering a non-invasive way to identify patients with poor prognosis before surgery.

papers.title: Dissecting genetic architecture and improving machine learning‑based genomic prediction of flowering time in Osmanthus fragrans by integrating structural variants.
papers.abstract: Sweet osmanthus (Osmanthus fragrans), a traditional ornamental plant in China, exhibits substantial variation in autumn flowering time, which significantly affects landscape application and cultivation efficiency. Here, we performed a genome-wide association study on 127 resequenced accessions classified into early, intermediate, and late flowering types, using a set of 2,325,410 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 246,824 structural variants (SVs). By integrating SNP/insertion and deletion (Indel) and SV data with weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine learning, and geno
papers.summary: This study dissects the genetic basis of flowering time variation in sweet osmanthus by combining genome-wide association analysis of SNPs and structural variants with gene co-expression networks and machine learning. Integrating structural variants improved the accuracy of genomic prediction models for flowering time, highlighting SVs as valuable markers beyond SNPs. The work provides both biological insights into flowering regulation and a practical framework for breeding ornamental plants.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a Five-Gene Metabolic Signature With Experimental Validation in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is hallmarked by profound metabolic reprogramming; however, its intricate crosstalk with the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and its clinical ramifications remain inadequately elucidated. This study aims to systematically decipher the metabolic-immune interplay in ccRCC through multi-omics integration, with the goal of identifying robust prognostic biomarkers and actionable therapeutic vulnerabilities.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to characterize the metabolic-immune crosstalk in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), identifying a five-gene metabolic signature with prognostic value. The signature was experimentally validated, suggesting potential utility as a biomarker and highlighting metabolic vulnerabilities for therapy.

papers.title: Machine learning approaches for cancer prognosis and diagnosis via non-coding RNA: a comprehensive review.
papers.abstract: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), once considered genomic dark matter, are now established as key regulators of gene expression with widespread roles in cellular homeostasis and disease. In cancer, ncRNA expression is frequently and systematically dysregulated, and many of these molecules circulate in stable, protected form within biofluids, offering a compelling basis for non-invasive or minimally invasive diagnostic strategies. However, their clinical translation remains substantially hindered to date due to biological complexity, technical noise, and high dimensionality inherent to ncRNA expression
papers.summary: This review surveys machine learning approaches that use non-coding RNA expression data for cancer diagnosis and prognosis. It highlights that ncRNAs are frequently dysregulated in cancer and can be detected in biofluids in stable forms, making them attractive non-invasive biomarkers, but their clinical translation is limited by biological complexity, technical noise, and high dimensionality.

papers.title: Adaptive deep learning for quantification and spatial distribution of abdominal adipose tissue from magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction in adults with a body mass index ≥24 kg/m2.
papers.abstract: Abdominal adipose tissue volume and spatial distribution are closely associated with a variety of metabolic diseases and reflect individual metabolic risk and health status. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility of an adaptive deep learning framework for the automated volumetric quantification and spatial mapping of visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) proton density fat fraction (PDFF) in adults with a body mass index (BMI) ≥24 kg/m2.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: This study evaluates an adaptive deep learning framework for automatically quantifying and spatially mapping visceral and subcutaneous abdominal adipose tissue from MRI proton density fat fraction (PDFF) scans in adults with a BMI ≥24 kg/m². The approach aims to enable reliable volumetric and spatial assessment of adipose distribution, which is linked to metabolic disease risk.

papers.title: LAMBDA: a prophage detection benchmark for genomic language models.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based genomic sequence models represent an emerging frontier in computational biology. Yet, their embeddings have not yet shown the same level of predictive power as natural and protein language models, highlighting a gap between current implementations and theoretical promise. Existing benchmarks for DNA language models primarily focus on classifying regulatory elements in eukaryotic genomes, leaving open the fundamental question of whether these models learn sequence-level features across whole genomes. We introduce LAMBDA, a benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate genome langu
papers.summary: LAMBDA is a new benchmark for evaluating genomic language models on prophage detection, a task that requires learning sequence-level features across whole genomes rather than just regulatory elements. It addresses the gap in assessing whether transformer-based DNA models capture broad genomic features, providing a rigorous test beyond eukaryotic regulatory classification.

papers.title: CAREPath: semantic context-aware reasoning paths with mechanism-augmented embeddings for drug repurposing.
papers.abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs that include drugs, genes, and diseases support drug repurposing by connecting drugs to diseases through gene-mediated multi-hop paths, thereby enabling mechanism-of-action reasoning. However, deeper traversal does not necessarily improve mechanistic reasoning: long paths grow combinatorially and frequently pass through hub genes, producing irrelevant gene regulatory signals, whereas overly constrained or sparse paths may miss broader biological context. We propose Context-Aware REasoning Path (CAREPath), a knowledge graph (KG)-large language model framework inspire
papers.summary: CAREPath is a knowledge graph–LLM framework for drug repurposing that addresses the trade-off between path depth and mechanistic relevance by using semantic context-aware reasoning paths with mechanism-augmented embeddings. It aims to avoid combinatorial explosion and hub-gene noise from long paths while still capturing broader biological context for connecting drugs to diseases via genes.

papers.title: DNAmBERT: a transformer-based model for non-invasive cancer diagnosis using DNA sequence and methylation data.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation alterations are early and stable hallmarks of cancer and represent promising biomarkers for non-invasive detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). However, current computational approaches often model DNA sequence and methylation features separately and struggle to capture complex read-level methylation architecture in heterogeneous, low-signal liquid biopsy data. Here, we present DNAmBERT, a Transformer-based deep learning framework designed to jointly model DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from cfDNA methylation sequencing data. DNA
papers.summary: DNAmBERT is a Transformer-based deep learning framework that jointly models DNA sequence context and read-level methylation haplotype structure from circulating cell-free DNA to enable non-invasive cancer diagnosis. Unlike prior approaches that treat sequence and methylation features separately, DNAmBERT captures complex read-level methylation architecture in low-signal liquid biopsy data, potentially improving early cancer detection.

papers.title: AResKGLM: a graph-grounded language-model framework for interpretable multi-hop antimicrobial resistance reasoning.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) threatens microbiology and microbiome bioinformatics because resistance phenotypes are shaped by interactions among genes, mobile genetic elements, and functional environments across microbial communities. Prioritizing resistance determinants requires models that reason across knowledge graphs (KGs) linking genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes. Existing graph-based methods compress this evidence into scalar scores, whereas large language models can produce explanations not grounded in structured evidence. We developed AResKGLM (Antimicrobial
papers.summary: AResKGLM is a framework that combines knowledge graphs of genes, proteins, pathways, drugs, and microbial phenotypes with large language models to reason about antimicrobial resistance. It aims to produce interpretable, multi-hop explanations for resistance phenotypes rather than opaque scalar scores, addressing a gap between graph-based methods and ungrounded LLM explanations.

papers.title: From rules to foundation models: a comprehensive review of machine learning approaches for siRNA design.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) are a clinically validated therapeutic modality with eight FDA-approved drugs, yet designing effective siRNAs remains computationally challenging due to complex dependencies on sequence composition, thermodynamic properties, target-site accessibility, and off-target interactions. Over two decades, computational approaches have evolved from empirical heuristics to deep learning systems integrating physical priors with learned representations. We review the complete landscape of machine learning methods for siRNA design, spanning classical scoring rules, pretraine
papers.summary: This review surveys two decades of computational methods for designing small interfering RNAs, tracing the evolution from simple empirical scoring rules to modern deep learning and foundation models that combine physical priors with learned representations. It covers the key factors affecting siRNA efficacy—sequence composition, thermodynamics, target accessibility, and off-target effects—and synthesizes the full landscape of machine learning approaches for this clinically validated therapeutic modality.

papers.title: Analysis of lipid-protein interactive oxidation and underlying pathways in aquatic products via multi-omics and machine learning: a case study of air-dried hairtail.
papers.abstract: The interactive oxidation mechanisms between lipids and proteins during aquatic product processing remain poorly understood, limiting quality control strategies. This investigation employed a comprehensive approach by integrating multi-omics data with seven machine learning models to elucidate the mechanisms of lipid and protein interactive oxidation in air-drying hairtail. The optimal XGBoost model achieved 0.98 AUC with 0.90 accuracy on test set. Machine learning combined with multi-omics has identified six oxidative biomarkers of lipid-protein interactions: receptor expression-enhancing pro
papers.summary: This study integrated multi-omics data with seven machine learning models to uncover how lipids and proteins interactively oxidize during air-drying of hairtail fish. The best model (XGBoost) achieved 0.98 AUC and 0.90 accuracy, identifying six oxidative biomarkers of lipid-protein interactions. The work offers a framework for quality control in aquatic product processing.

papers.title: Identifying unmet needs in food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome using search query analysis and a large language model.
papers.abstract: Food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) is a non-IgE-mediated food allergy with many unanswered clinical and research questions. Existing educational resources, patient-facing education materials, and guidelines may not fully reflect families' information needs. Digital data and artificial intelligence (AI) offer new ways to identify public concerns in rare diseases.
papers.journal: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. Global
papers.summary: This study uses search query analysis combined with a large language model to identify unmet information needs among families affected by food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES), a rare non-IgE-mediated food allergy. The approach reveals gaps between existing educational resources and the actual concerns of patients and caregivers, demonstrating how digital data and AI can surface public priorities in rare diseases.

papers.title: DyAb: sequence-based antibody design and property prediction in a low-data regime.
papers.abstract: Protein therapeutic design and property prediction are frequently hampered by data scarcity. Here we propose a model, DyAb, that addresses these issues by leveraging a pair-wise representation to predict differences in binding affinity, rather than absolute values. DyAb is built on top of a pre-trained protein language model and achieves a Spearman rank correlation of up to 0.85 on binding affinity prediction across monoclonal antibodies targeting three different antigens (EGFR, IL-6, and an internal target), given as few as 100 training data. We employ DyAb in two design contexts: as a rankin
papers.summary: DyAb is a sequence-based model that predicts relative binding affinity differences between antibody variants rather than absolute values, leveraging a pre-trained protein language model and pairwise representations. It achieves Spearman correlations up to 0.85 across three antigen targets (EGFR, IL-6, and an internal target) using as few as 100 training examples, and is applied to antibody ranking and design tasks. This demonstrates that low-data antibody property prediction can be effective when framed as a pairwise comparison problem.

papers.title: HelixCross - Design and development of an AI-powered cross-examination simulation for forensic expert testimony training.
papers.abstract: Forensic testimony is where science meets the courtroom, and it is one of the critical forensic skills taught largely by apprenticeship. An examiner who overstates a match, mishandles a probability, or cannot support a method under direct or cross-examination can weaken the evidence in precisely the cases that rely on it. Yet in most forensic laboratories, testimony preparation remains largely informal, mentor-dependent, and unscalable. Consequently, many practitioners first face rigorous cross-examination at trial. To address this gap, HelixCross, an alpha-stage, publicly accessible, prompt-e
papers.summary: HelixCross is an AI-powered simulation tool designed to help forensic examiners practice cross-examination for expert testimony. It addresses the lack of scalable, formal training by providing a publicly accessible platform for realistic questioning practice. The tool aims to improve how forensic scientists handle scrutiny of their evidence in court.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of DNA damage response-related markers in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma using machine learning approaches.
papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks reliable prognostic biomarkers. Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) has been implicated in genomic instability across multiple cancers, but its prognostic significance in ESCC remains unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate HRD score as a prognostic biomarker and develop a machine learning-based predictive model for ESCC.
papers.summary: This study evaluates homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) scores as a prognostic biomarker in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), a cancer lacking reliable prognostic markers. The authors use machine learning to build a predictive model incorporating DNA damage response-related markers, aiming to improve risk stratification for ESCC patients.

papers.title: A CFH- and SPINT2-based prognostic signature for cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a highly malignant tumor with a poor prognosis, and reliable biomarkers for postoperative risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a CFH- and SPINT2-based prognostic signature to support postoperative risk stratification and inform adjuvant therapy selection in CCA through integrative machine learning and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.summary: This study develops a prognostic signature for cholangiocarcinoma based on the expression of two genes, CFH and SPINT2, using machine learning combined with single-cell transcriptomics. The signature is intended to help stratify postoperative risk and guide decisions about adjuvant therapy in this highly malignant cancer with poor prognosis.

papers.title: A token-pruning framework enables efficient representation of the human genome for RNA modification analysis.
papers.abstract: Modelling long genomic sequences remains challenging due to extreme sequence length, high redundancy, and the need for biological interpretability. Although Transformer-based architectures have achieved strong performance across genomic tasks, their high computational cost and reliance on fixed tokenization strategies limit their scalability and ability to focus on biologically informative regions.
papers.summary: The authors propose a token-pruning framework that reduces redundancy in long genomic sequences, enabling more efficient Transformer-based modelling of the human genome. They apply it to RNA modification analysis, showing that pruning tokens improves scalability while preserving biologically informative regions and interpretability.

papers.title: Rational and computation-assisted engineering of a compact and efficient CRISPR-Cas12f genome editor.
papers.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas12f system is an ultracompact genome-editing platform, yet only a few orthologs exhibit robust activity in mammalian cells. Here, we systematically screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, capable of genome editing in human cells. sgRNA scaffold optimization enhanced the basal activity of PspCas12f1. To further improve its performance, we combined structure-guided rational design with protein language model-assisted filtering. Candidate mutations predicted by SaProt were further screened based on structural proximity to the DNA-b
papers.journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
papers.summary: This study screened 23 Cas12f orthologs and identified two active nucleases, PspCas12f1 and TcCas12f1, that can edit genomes in human cells. By optimizing the sgRNA scaffold and combining structure-guided design with a protein language model (SaProt), the authors engineered a compact, highly efficient Cas12f genome editor suitable for therapeutic applications.

papers.title: A computational framework integrating a protein language model with alchemical simulation for gain-of-function enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Engineering enzymes with enhanced activity and stability is a central goal of biotechnology, yet the inherent trade-off between optimizing global protein fitness and specific substrate binding affinity poses a significant challenge. Here, we present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that synergistically integrates a fine-tuned protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) to overcome this limitation. Our workflow employs a parameter-efficient fine-tuned ESM-2 model to perform high-throughput saturation mutagenesis, rapidly identifying mutations that preserve protein fi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-FEP, a computational framework that combines a fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language model with alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) simulations to design gain-of-function enzymes. The language model rapidly screens saturation mutagenesis libraries for mutations that preserve global protein fitness, while FEP then evaluates specific substrate binding affinity, addressing the trade-off between overall stability and catalytic activity. This hybrid approach aims to make enzyme engineering more efficient by narrowing the search space before expensive physics-based calculations.

papers.title: scProtoTransformer: Scalable reference mapping across molecules, cells, and donors.
papers.abstract: The rapid accumulation of single-cell data has made it possible to comprehensively characterize biological systems at molecular, cellular, and donor levels. However, scalable reference mapping across different resolutions remains a major challenge in current research. Here, we propose scProtoTransformer, a prototype-based Transformer architecture designed to achieve scalable reference mapping across molecular, cell, and donor levels. scProtoTransformer introduces a knowledge-guided prototype tokenizer that projects gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes, effectively
papers.summary: scProtoTransformer is a prototype-based Transformer model that maps new single-cell data onto existing reference atlases at molecular, cellular, and donor resolutions. It uses a knowledge-guided tokenizer that converts gene expression into biologically interpretable pathway prototypes, enabling scalable reference mapping. This addresses a key bottleneck in leveraging the growing accumulation of single-cell data.

papers.title: Programmable protein degraders enable selective knockdown of pathogenic β-catenin subpopulations in vitro and in vivo.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of Wnt signaling results in unregulated accumulation of cytosolic β-catenin, which subsequently enters the nucleus and promotes transcription of genes that contribute to cellular proliferation and malignancy. Here, we sought to eliminate pathogenic β-catenin from the cytosol using designer ubiquibodies (uAbs), chimeric proteins composed of an E3 ubiquitin ligase and a target-binding domain that redirect intracellular proteins to the proteasome for degradation. To accelerate uAb development, we leveraged a protein language model-driven algorithm called SaLT&PepPr to computat
papers.summary: This study engineers 'ubiquibodies' (uAbs), chimeric proteins combining an E3 ubiquitin ligase with a target-binding domain, to selectively degrade pathogenic cytosolic β-catenin that drives aberrant Wnt signaling. Using the protein language model-based algorithm SaLT&PepPr to design the binding domains, the authors achieved selective knockdown of β-catenin subpopulations both in vitro and in vivo. This demonstrates a programmable protein degradation strategy for targeting specific oncogenic protein pools.

papers.title: Integrating AI and Molecular Modeling for Structural Prediction of a Closed-Pore State of the hERG Channel.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated potassium channel hERG (Kv11.1) plays a central role in cardiac repolarisation by mediating the rapid delayed rectifier K+ current (IKr). Blockage of hERG by small molecules can lead to delayed repolarisation, QT interval prolongation, and potentially fatal arrhythmias, making the channel a critical focus in drug safety screening. Despite extensive pharmacological and electrophysiological characterization, a complete structural understanding of hERG gating remains limited by the absence of an experimentally determined closed-state structure. Here, we use AI-based structural m
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors used AI-based structure prediction combined with molecular modeling to generate a model of the closed-pore state of the hERG potassium channel, a key cardiac ion channel implicated in drug-induced arrhythmias. Since no experimental closed-state structure exists, this computational model fills a gap in understanding hERG gating and could aid drug safety screening.

papers.title: ESMDynamic: Fast and accurate prediction of protein dynamic contact maps from single sequences.
papers.abstract: Understanding conformational dynamics is essential for elucidating protein function, yet most deep learning models in structural biology predict only static structures. Here, we present ESMDynamic, a deep learning model that predicts residue-residue contact dynamics directly from protein sequence. Built on the ESMFold architecture and trained on conformational variability from experimental structure ensembles and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, ESMDynamic predicts dynamic contact probabilities, contact occupancy fraction, and coarse-grained kinetics of contact formation and dissociation a
papers.summary: ESMDynamic is a deep learning model that predicts protein residue-residue contact dynamics directly from a single sequence, building on the ESMFold architecture. It is trained on conformational variability from experimental structure ensembles and molecular dynamics simulations, and outputs dynamic contact probabilities, contact occupancy fractions, and coarse-grained kinetics of contact formation and dissociation. This enables fast, accurate prediction of protein dynamics without requiring multiple sequence alignments or expensive simulations.

papers.title: CAKR: commutative algebra k-mer representations for genomics.
papers.abstract: Despite the availability of various sequence analysis models, comparative genomic analysis remains a challenge in genomics, genetics, and phylogenetics. Commutative algebra, a fundamental tool in algebraic geometry and number theory, has rarely been used in data and biological sciences. In this study, we introduce commutative algebra k-mer representations as a nonlinear algebraic framework for analyzing genomic sequences. This representation bridges commutative algebra, algebraic topology, combinatorics, and machine learning to establish a mathematical framework for comparative genomic analysi
papers.summary: The authors introduce CAKR, a framework that represents genomic sequences as k-mer objects using commutative algebra, bridging algebraic topology, combinatorics, and machine learning for comparative genomics. This provides a new mathematical foundation for sequence comparison tasks in genomics, genetics, and phylogenetics.

papers.title: Environmental PFOA exposure and the risk of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: An integrated computational toxicology and multi-omics study.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), a pervasive environmental pollutant, has been implicated in hepatic injury and metabolic dysfunction. However, its role as an environmental risk factor in the pathogenesis of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) remains incompletely understood, particularly from a systems biology perspective.
papers.summary: This study integrates computational toxicology with multi-omics data to investigate whether environmental exposure to PFOA contributes to the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). By combining systems-level modeling with molecular profiling, the authors identify potential mechanisms linking PFOA exposure to liver metabolic dysfunction.

papers.title: Development of a PCR-based technique for genotyping UGT1A1 gene and distribution of rs3064744 alleles in the Russian population.
papers.abstract: Accurate determination of tandem thymine-adenine (TA) repeat numbers in the UGT1A1 promoter region (rs3064744) is essential for diagnosing Gilbert's syndrome and personalizing therapy with toxic agents like irinotecan and atazanavir. However, traditional polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays face severe limitations due to the AT-rich sequence and overlapping melting temperatures (Tm) of the highly homologous 7TA and 8TA alleles. In this context, melting curve analysis (MCA) employing fluorophore-quencher systems has emerged as a promising alternative. The purpose of this study was to develop
papers.summary: This study developed a PCR-based genotyping assay using melting curve analysis with fluorophore-quencher probes to accurately distinguish TA repeat alleles (rs3064744) in the UGT1A1 promoter, overcoming the difficulty of resolving the highly homologous 7TA and 8TA variants. The authors then applied this method to characterize the distribution of these alleles in the Russian population, providing a tool relevant to Gilbert's syndrome diagnosis and personalized dosing of drugs like irinotecan and atazanavir.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-driven identification and mechanistic exploration of synergistic anti-aging compounds from Dengzhan Shengmai formulation.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple dysregulated pathways, and synergistic compound combinations offer distinct therapeutic advantages through multi-target and multi-pathway interactions. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations are inherently synergistic, yet systematically identifying their active anti-aging combinations remains a major challenge. Here, we developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning-based framework integrating molecular descriptors, ADMET parameters, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) network embeddings learned via a variational graph auto-encoder (VGA
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepSMCA, a deep learning framework that combines molecular descriptors, ADMET properties, and protein-protein interaction network embeddings from a variational graph auto-encoder to identify synergistic anti-aging compound combinations from the traditional Chinese medicine formulation Dengzhan Shengmai. This approach offers a systematic way to uncover multi-target, multi-pathway active combinations from complex herbal formulations.

papers.title: Etiology-Specific Nomograms for Predicting First Variceal Bleeding in Decompensated HBV- and HCV-Related Cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: Patients with decompensated hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related cirrhosis are at high risk of first variceal bleeding, yet etiology-specific and stage-specific prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate nomogram models for predicting the risk of first variceal bleeding in this population.
papers.summary: This study develops and internally validates etiology-specific nomograms to predict the risk of first variceal bleeding in patients with decompensated HBV- and HCV-related cirrhosis. The models aim to fill a gap in stage- and etiology-specific risk prediction for this high-risk population.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage population that shows high transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) activity. Using single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niche analysis, and machine learning, the authors link genetic susceptibility to a pathogenic immune cell program in the liver. The work bridges genetic risk with cell-type-specific mechanisms, potentially highlighting new therapeutic targets for PSC.

papers.title: Machine learning-based early identification of heart failure/congestion complicating acute coronary syndrome using body composition analysis: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a major complication of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and is associated with poor outcomes.
papers.summary: This retrospective cohort study uses machine learning applied to body composition analysis to identify heart failure or congestion early in patients with acute coronary syndrome. The approach aims to improve early detection of this major complication, which is linked to poor outcomes.

papers.title: Preventing relapse in ulcerative colitis remission maintenance: machine learning prediction and reinforcement-learning herbal prescription optimization with external validation.
papers.abstract: Maintaining remission in ulcerative colitis (UC) with traditional Chinese herbal medicine is challenging because fixed-intensity prescriptions may not accommodate changes in inflammatory burden. This study aimed to predict 52-week relapse and develop a data-driven policy for sequential adjustment of herbal treatment intensity.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to predict 52-week relapse in ulcerative colitis patients in remission and applies reinforcement learning to optimize sequential adjustments of traditional Chinese herbal medicine treatment intensity. The approach is externally validated, suggesting a data-driven framework for personalized remission maintenance.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification and experimental validation of key biomarkers in the bile acid metabolic pathway associated with ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Bile acids are shown to participate in inflammatory responses. This study was designed to investigate the functions of bile acid metabolism-associated genes (BAMGs) in ulcerative colitis (UC), identify the potential biomarkers based on eleven machine learning algorithms.
papers.summary: This study applies eleven machine learning algorithms to identify bile acid metabolism-associated genes as potential biomarkers for ulcerative colitis, then validates the top candidates experimentally. The work links bile acid metabolic pathway dysregulation to UC pathogenesis and nominates specific genes as candidate biomarkers.

papers.title: Immune-Like Malignant Epithelial Programs Shape Tumor-Immune Interactions and Inform Prognostic Stratification in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is characterized by marked cellular heterogeneity, yet how malignant epithelial states contribute to immune regulation and clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data to map the cellular landscape of LUAD and identify malignant epithelial cells based on inferred copy-number alterations. Epithelial states were further examined through trajectory inference, transcription factor analysis, and cell-cell communication profiling. Single-cell-derived genes were subsequently integrated with TCGA and independent GEO cohorts to
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-sequencing data to map the cellular landscape of lung adenocarcinoma, identifying malignant epithelial cells via inferred copy-number alterations. It characterizes epithelial states through trajectory inference, transcription factor analysis, and cell-cell communication profiling, revealing immune-like malignant epithelial programs that shape tumor-immune interactions. These single-cell-derived signatures are then integrated with TCGA and GEO cohorts to inform prognostic stratification.

papers.title: Bioinformatics Screening and Preliminary Experimental Verification of Integrated Stress Response-Associated MYC and BAG3 in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has high morbidity and mortality, and integrated stress response (ISR) participates in its progression. Traditional COPD diagnosis relies mainly on GOLD criteria, while ISR-based auxiliary molecular markers are still lacking. This study aimed to comprehensively analyze and identify ISR-related biomarkers in COPD, and to uncover their underlying molecular mechanisms.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study uses bioinformatics screening combined with preliminary experimental validation to identify integrated stress response (ISR)-associated biomarkers in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), highlighting MYC and BAG3 as key candidates. The work aims to address the lack of ISR-based molecular markers for COPD diagnosis beyond traditional GOLD criteria.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning analysis of the impact of tranexamic acid combined with antibiotics on renal function and its risk factors in hip replacement surgeries.
papers.abstract: Early prediction of renal function changes in patients undergoing hip replacement surgery enables timely intervention for acute kidney injury and acute renal failure, which in turn improves treatment outcomes. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning model that uses real-world clinical parameters to predict postoperative renal function changes. The model incorporates tranexamic acid (TXA) and antibiotics as key predictive factors, examines their combined effect on renal function, and identifies associated risk factors.
papers.summary: This study develops an interpretable machine learning model to predict postoperative renal function changes in hip replacement patients, incorporating tranexamic acid and antibiotics as key predictors. The model aims to enable early identification of acute kidney injury risk and associated risk factors using real-world clinical parameters.

papers.title: Transcriptomic profiling reveals immune signatures associated with potential COVID-19 susceptibility and a predictive framework in a Chinese cohort.
papers.abstract: Despite significant interindividual susceptibility to COVID-19, the molecular basis of host vulnerability in the Chinese population remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study profiles transcriptomes in a Chinese cohort to identify immune gene expression signatures linked to individual differences in COVID-19 susceptibility. The authors use these signatures to build a predictive framework for identifying individuals at higher risk of infection or severe outcomes.

papers.title: Interpretable prediction of nucleic acid-binding proteins using a protein language model.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) and RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) is critical for elucidating transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms. However, existing computational approaches often rely on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations, which limit the subsequent generalizability.
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable method for predicting DNA- and RNA-binding proteins using a protein language model, aiming to avoid reliance on inferred labels or domain-specific annotations that limit generalizability. The approach leverages learned protein representations to identify nucleic acid-binding proteins more broadly.

papers.title: DeepVIC: modular prediction and classification of bacterial virulence factors using protein language model embeddings.
papers.abstract: Virulence factors (VFs) play critical roles in bacterial pathogenesis, and identifying these proteins and elucidating their mechanisms is essential for developing effective infection treatments. While protein language models (PLMs) have revolutionized the protein analysis, current in silico methods for classifying VFs primarily rely on fine-tuned PLMs ProtBert-BFD that perform identification and classification in a single step. This monolithic approach lacks flexibility and is vulnerable to error propagation, particularly from false negatives. Moreover, the direct use of PLM embeddings as feat
papers.summary: DeepVIC is a modular tool that predicts bacterial virulence factors and classifies them into functional categories using protein language model embeddings. By separating identification from classification, it avoids the error propagation and inflexibility of monolithic fine-tuned PLM approaches like ProtBert-BFD.

papers.title: Computational mapping of resistance-relevant signals in proteins using deep and classical feature spaces.
papers.abstract: The functional diversity of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins necessitates advanced computational frameworks capable of capturing complex macromolecular signatures beyond simple sequence homology. While traditional alignment-based tools identify known resistance determinants, they often overlook the underlying biochemical and structural properties that define novel or divergent resistant macromolecules.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that combines deep learning and classical feature representations to map resistance-relevant signals in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) proteins, moving beyond simple sequence homology. The approach aims to capture complex biochemical and structural signatures that could help identify novel or divergent resistance determinants missed by traditional alignment-based tools.

papers.title: SA-FGPN: Stability-aware feature-gated progressive learning for pediatric brain tumor classification from high dimensional gene expression data.
papers.abstract: Accurate pediatric brain tumor classification from gene expression data remains challenging due to the extremely high-dimensional nature of transcriptomic datasets, where tens of thousands of features are available from only a limited number of samples. This imbalance increases the risk of overfitting, unstable feature selection, and unreliable performance estimation. Moreover, molecular heterogeneity among pediatric brain tumor subtypes makes robust prediction and biological interpretation difficult. This study aims to develop a stable and interpretable deep learning framework for pediatric b
papers.summary: The authors introduce SA-FGPN, a deep learning framework designed to classify pediatric brain tumor subtypes from high-dimensional gene expression data despite very small sample sizes. The method uses stability-aware feature gating and progressive learning to reduce overfitting and improve feature selection reliability. It aims to provide both robust predictions and interpretable biological insights into tumor heterogeneity.

papers.title: Cross-residual knowledge graph learning for robust multi-trait gene-trait prioritization in rice.
papers.abstract: Prioritizing genes associated with agronomic traits remains challenging because relevant evidence is distributed across heterogeneous biological resources and curated gene-trait associations are incomplete.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a cross-residual knowledge graph learning approach to prioritize genes linked to agronomic traits in rice, addressing the challenge of integrating heterogeneous biological data and incomplete gene-trait associations. The method aims to improve robustness in multi-trait gene prioritization, potentially aiding crop improvement efforts.

papers.title: Computational Characterization of Pathogenic LMNA Missense Variants: Structural Instability, Altered Binding, and Conformational Dynamics.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the LMNA gene underlie a broad spectrum of laminopathies, including muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and premature aging syndromes; however, the molecular mechanisms by which missense variants disrupt Lamin A structural integrity remain incompletely characterized. Systematic computational approaches for prioritizing pathogenic variants and elucidating their structural consequences are critically needed.
papers.summary: This study uses computational structural analysis to characterize how missense mutations in the LMNA gene disrupt Lamin A protein stability, binding interactions, and conformational dynamics. The authors aim to provide a systematic framework for prioritizing pathogenic variants underlying laminopathies such as muscular dystrophies and premature aging syndromes.

papers.title: InfoMedex: drug-drug interaction prediction via a multimodal CNN-transformer model.
papers.abstract: Drug-drug interactions are an important source of preventable adverse drug events. Computational methods that incorporate chemical structure and biological context may support more scalable and interpretable interaction prediction.
papers.journal: Frontiers in drug safety and regulation
papers.summary: InfoMedex introduces a multimodal deep learning model that combines CNN and transformer architectures to predict drug-drug interactions by integrating chemical structure and biological context information. The approach aims to provide more scalable and interpretable DDI prediction than existing computational methods, potentially helping reduce preventable adverse drug events.

papers.title: MetaCYP: a unified framework for prediction of cytochrome P450 metabolic sites and reaction types via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are the predominant drug-metabolizing proteins in humans, collectively governing the structural transformation of drugs and xenobiotics while directly shaping their pharmacological activity and toxicological profiles. Accurate prediction of CYP-substrate reaction sites and reaction types is therefore central to drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment. Existing computational models, however, largely depend on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, constraining their generalization across CYP isoforms.
papers.summary: MetaCYP is a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the metabolic sites and reaction types of cytochrome P450 enzymes, which are the main drug-metabolizing proteins in humans. Unlike prior models that rely on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, MetaCYP aims to generalize better across different CYP isoforms, supporting drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-integrated multimodal retinal imaging for early detection and risk stratification of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.abstract: We developed and validated RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework for simultaneous risk stratification of hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative-associated retinal changes from integrated fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata.
papers.summary: The authors developed RetinalVNG-Net, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates fundus photography, optical coherence tomography, and clinical metadata to simultaneously stratify risk for hypertensive retinopathy, diabetic retinopathy, and neurodegenerative-associated retinal changes. This approach aims to enable early detection and risk assessment of systemic vascular and neurodegenerative diseases through retinal imaging.
